Main.sentence: The Joyce Foundation is a ___E:non-operating private foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foundation_(United_States_law)#Private_foundation)___ based in ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ , ___E:Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois)___ .
As of 2025, it had assets of approximately $1.24 billion.

President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ served on the foundation's board of directors from 1994 through 2002. The Joyce Foundation is notable for its support of ___E:gun control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_politics_in_the_United_States)___ measures.
The Joyce Foundation was established in 1948 by Beatrice Joyce Kean of Chicago.

She was the sole heir of ___E:David Joyce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Joyce_(businessman))___ , a lumber executive and industrialist from ___E:Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton,_Iowa)___ , ___E:Iowa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa)___ .

The family wealth came from the lumber industry, including family-owned timberlands, plywood and saw mills, and wholesale and retail building material distribution facilities located in the ___E:Midwest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States)___ , ___E:Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana)___ , and ___E:Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas)___ .
The Foundation was modestly endowed until Kean's death in 1972, when she bequeathed it nearly $100 million.
Charles U. Daly, a former aide to President ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ , served as president of the Foundation for eight years.

He was succeeded by Craig Kennedy in 1986.  Deborah Leff, a trial lawyer for the civil rights division of the ___E:Department of Justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice)___ , served as president of the organization from 1992 to 1999, and was succeeded by ___E:Paula DiPerna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_DiPerna)___ , named president in 1999.  DiPerna was succeeded in 2002 by Ellen S. Alberding, the organization's seventh president.
President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ served on the foundation's board of directors from 1994 through 2002.
The Joyce Foundation is one of the few private foundations that considers ___E:gun violence related U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_violence_in_the_United_States)___ research proposals.
Joyce distributes grants designed to prevent gun violence by reducing the accessibility of firearms.
Since 1993, the Joyce Foundation spent over $54 million on over 100 grants that favor gun control.
